title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft sheet, headed '6-41' and 'n° 392' (a Bourbaki rédaction number), apparently reused as scrap paper inside the L-function notes. It is the first exercise of §5 of a draft chapter of Commutative Algebra, probably ch. VII 'Diviseurs' or an early version of it.

Setting: A is a noetherian integrally closed domain with fraction field K. L/K is a finite extension of degree n, and B is the integral closure of A in L, assumed finite over A. A ⊂ E ⊂ F ⊂ B are intermediate rings.

(a) Height-one primes go up and down along the finite integral extensions E ⊂ F. Over a height-one prime p of E there are finitely many primes P of F, all of height one. Conversely P ∩ E has height one. The tools are going-up, incomparability and the dimension formula for finite extensions of A.

(b) Degrees are defined as follows.
- For a height-one prime P of F, deg_E(P) = [Frac(F/P) : Frac(E/(P∩E))]; it is 0 for other primes.
- For a P-primary ideal Q, deg_E(Q) = m·deg_E(P), where m is the least integer with P^(m) ⊂ Q.
- For an ideal a ≠ 0, deg_E(a) is the sum over the isolated primary components of a.

An ideal a of C (A ⊂ C ⊂ B) is called pseudo-invertible if a_p is invertible in the semi-local ring C_p for every height-one prime p of A. This is invertibility in codimension one. The exercise asks to show that a ≠ 0 is pseudo-invertible iff deg_C(a) = Σ_P n(P) deg_C(P), where div(aB) = Σ n(P) P over height-one primes of B.

The hint runs as follows. Localize so that A is a DVR; then C is one-dimensional semi-local and B is a semi-local PID. Invertible ideals are then principal. For a = xC, deg_C(a) should equal ℓ_C(C/xC) = ℓ_C(B/xB); the second equality holds because B/C has finite length and x is a non-zero-divisor. Prime avoidance gives y ∈ a with y ∉ C ∩ a m_i B for all i, hence yB = aB. The final remark is that every nonzero ideal of B is pseudo-invertible.

The purpose is a local criterion comparing an ideal of a non-normal order C with its extension to the normalization B. This is the classical theory of ideals in orders and conductors, presumably serving Bourbaki's treatment of divisors. It has no visible link to the surrounding L-function computations: the previous and next pages compute ξ_E(1/qt) = A(t) ε'(E) ξ_E(t).
errors: With the definition via symbolic powers, deg_C(xC) is in general NOT the length of C/xC when C is not regular, so the hint (and hence the criterion as stated) fails. Example: A = k[[t^2]], B = k[[t]], C = k[[t^2,t^3]], x = t^4. Here ℓ_C(C/t^4C) = 4 = ℓ(B/t^4B) = Σ n(P)deg_C(P). But the least m with m^m ⊂ t^4C is m = 3, since t^5 ∈ m^2 \ t^4C and m^3 ⊂ t^4C. So the principal (invertible) ideal t^4C has deg_C = 3 ≠ 4. The correct definition of deg_C(Q) should be the length ℓ(C_P/Q_P) weighted by the residue degree (multiplicity / length), not the symbolic-power exponent. The two coincide only when C_P is a DVR. Presumably the published Bourbaki version corrects this; unsure.
The parenthetical 'deg_F(Q) = m' is consistent with the definition but trivial, since deg_F(P) = 1.

ideas.what: Height-one primes are preserved up and down in finite integral extensions between a normal noetherian domain and its finite integral closure
ideas.modern_name: Going-up / incomparability / dimension formula for finite extensions
ideas.where_published: Standard (Bourbaki AC V, VII; EGA IV §5 in general form)

ideas.what: Pseudo-invertible ideals (invertible in codimension one) in an order C between A and its normalization B, characterized by comparing degree/length of a with the divisor of aB
ideas.modern_name: Local criterion for invertibility of ideals in one-dimensional orders via lengths (ℓ(C/xC) = ℓ(B/xB))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical theory of orders (Dedekind, Krull); Bourbaki Algèbre commutative ch. VII exercises
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative (exercises, likely ch. VII); this is a Bourbaki draft, not a Grothendieck text

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed Bourbaki draft exercise on routine commutative algebra, reused as scrap paper. Its only point of interest is a genuine error in the draft definition of degree (symbolic-power exponent instead of length), which is archival trivia rather than missed mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially accurate. In 'y ∉ C ∩ (a m_i B)' the image reads '(am_i B)', consistent with the transcription.
The handwritten '29' in the lower left margin is the archive page number, not part of the text.
